paragraphs.text: Strategic Role: Globally recognized as the manufacturing, processing, and financial price-discovery capital of guar gum. Handles over 70% of India's refined splits and finished gum powders.

Key Facilities: Over 120 automated splitting and high-capacity powder manufacturing facilities in the Basni, Boranada, and Mandore Industrial Areas (Jodhpur) and the Bichhwal and Karni Industrial Areas (Bikaner) (e.g., Vikas WSP, Sunita Hydrocolloids, Hindustan Gum & Chemicals, Neelkanth Polymers); specialized chemical derivatization plants and advanced R&D laboratories measuring rotational viscosity via Fann and Brookfield viscometers.
Catchment Areas: The entire Thar Desert production basin: Bikaner, Barmer, Jodhpur, Jaisalmer, Nagaur, Churu, and interstate receipts from western Haryana.

summary.text: In Indian agricultural and commodity trade economics (Directorate of Economics & Statistics / ICAR-CAZRI Jodhpur / NCDEX), Guar Seed (Cyamopsis tetragonoloba, Cluster Bean / Gwar) is an industrial cash-legume and export crop. India holds a near-monopoly on global production, accounting for roughly 80% to 85% of total world guar seed and guar gum output, with Pakistan supplying the bulk of the remainder.

protection.name: Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB) (Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. cyamopsidis)
protection.geography: All-India Commercial Belts (Heavy in wet monsoon spells)
protection.impact: Systemic seed-borne infection; small, water-soaked, translucent spots on leaves; spots turn dark brown, angular, and necrotic with yellow chlorotic borders; lesions extend down petioles to the main stem (black stem streaks); plants wilt, collapse, and drop leaves prematurely (severe defoliation); causes 20–50% seed loss.
protection.passage: Guarseed — source table 153, row 2. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Alternaria Leaf Spot / Blight (Alternaria cyamopsidis)
protection.impact: Dark brown, circular-to-irregular spots with distinct concentric rings on leaves; lesions coalesce into large necrotic blights; leaves become brittle, curl, and dry up prematurely; pods develop sunken dark brown spots with shriveled seeds.
protection.passage: Guarseed — source table 153, row 3. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Powdery Mildew (Erysiphe polygoni, Leveillula taurica)
protection.geography: Cool Autumn Weather (Late Season in all belts)
protection.impact: White, talcum-powder-like fungal mycelium appears on upper leaf surfaces and stems; spreads across the entire canopy, turning leaves dull grey-white; causes premature foliar drying and incomplete pod filling.
protection.passage: Guarseed — source table 153, row 4. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Sucking Pest Complex: Jassids & Whiteflies (Empoasca kerri, Bemisia tabaci)
protection.impact:
Jassids: Nymphs and adults suck sap from leaf undersides, injecting toxic saliva; margins turn yellow, curl down, turn reddish-brown, and dry up ("Hopper Burn").

Whiteflies: Vector for viral infections; exude sticky honeydew that fosters black sooty mold.
protection.passage: Guarseed — source table 153, row 5. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Root Rot & Wilt (Rhizoctonia solani, Fusarium solani)
protection.impact: Dark, sunken, water-soaked brown lesions on lower stems and root collars; roots decay into a brown fibrous mush; plants wilt and collapse in circular patches across fields subject to poor drainage.
protection.passage: Guarseed — source table 153, row 6. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Pulse Beetle / Bruchid (Callosobruchus chinensis)
protection.impact: Adult beetles lay white eggs on dried seed coats; grubs burrow inside, feeding on the protein-rich germ and endosperm, leaving circular exit holes; reduces test weight, seed germination, and split recovery.
protection.passage: Guarseed — source table 153, row 7. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.
